name: Lithuania
description: Lithuania offers expats a compelling blend of affordability, opportunity, and a high quality of life within the European Union. It's particularly appealing for professionals, remote workers, and families seeking economic stability and a supportive environment. The country combines modern infrastructure with rich cultural experiences and abundant natural beauty.
longdescription: Lithuania, a Baltic state in Northeastern Europe, has become an increasingly attractive destination for expatriates due to its growing economy, competitive salaries, and lower cost of living compared to many Western European countries. The country boasts a modern public healthcare system and a high quality of life, consistently ranking well in global indexes. Its capital, Vilnius, is a vibrant city known for its Baroque architecture, tech innovation, and youthful energy, offering a thriving cultural scene with numerous festivals and events. While the economy has seen significant growth since gaining independence, opportunities are particularly strong in sectors like IT, fintech, engineering, and business services, with a demand for skilled foreign workers. The society is generally welcoming, though the Lithuanian language can be a barrier, and there's a strong sense of national pride. The climate is continental, with warm summers and cold, dark winters. The government promotes start-ups and international investment through simplified regulations and tax advantages. Overall, Lithuania provides a secure, family-friendly environment with a good work-life balance and a strong sense of community, making it appealing for a diverse range of expats.

visas.name: National Visa (Type D) for Work/Employment
visas.description: The National Visa (Type D) for Work/Employment in Lithuania is for non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals intending to stay and work in Lithuania for a period longer than 90 days, typically up to one year. It serves as an initial authorization for employment and a bridge to obtaining a temporary residence permit for longer-term stays.
visas.target_applicant: Third-country nationals who have secured a job offer from a Lithuanian employer and possess the necessary qualifications and work authorization.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The National Visa (D) serves as an initial entry and work authorization. For longer stays and a path to permanent residency, visa holders must apply for a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP) from the Migration Department, usually issued for up to two years and renewable.
visas.renewal_conditions: A National Visa (D) cannot be renewed or extended. For continued stay and work beyond one year, applicants typically need to transition to a Temporary Residence Permit. A new national visa may be issued if more than 180 days have passed since the previous one expired.
benefits: Allows legal entry and stay in Lithuania for more than 90 days.
Grants authorization to work in Lithuania for the visa's validity period.
Provides a pathway to apply for a temporary residence permit for extended stays.
Permits multiple entries into Lithuania during its validity, if issued as such.
Allows short-term travel within the Schengen Area under applicable rules.
required_documents: Completed National Visa (D) application form (electronically via MIGRIS)
Valid passport or travel document (valid for at least 3 months beyond visa duration, issued within last 10 years, with at least 2 blank pages)
One recent color passport-sized photograph (35 x 45 mm, white background)
Proof of financial resources/income (e.g., employment contract, bank statement) sufficient for living expenses and return funds
Proof of health insurance valid in Lithuania and all Schengen countries, with at least €30,000 coverage
A valid work permit issued by the Lithuanian Labour Exchange (Užimtumo tarnyba)
Copy of the employment contract
Mediation letter from the employer (submitted electronically via MIGRIS)
Proof of qualifications for the job (e.g., diplomas, training certificates, employment record proving 1 year experience in the sector)
Police clearance certificate (issued no earlier than six months before application date)
Proof of accommodation in Lithuania
application_process_steps: Secure a job offer from a Lithuanian company.
Employer applies for a work permit from the Lithuanian Labour Exchange and submits a mediation letter electronically via MIGRIS.
Employee completes the National Visa (D) application form electronically through the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS) and uploads digital copies of required documents.
Book an appointment at a Lithuanian diplomatic mission, consular office, or external service provider (e.g., VFS Global) if abroad, or the Migration Department if legally in Lithuania.
Pay the application fee.
Attend the appointment, submit biometric data, and provide original copies of the attached application documents.
Await the decision on the visa application.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Employment
visas.description: The Temporary Residence Permit for Employment in Lithuania allows non-EU/EEA citizens to reside and work in Lithuania based on an employment contract with a Lithuanian company. It is typically issued for up to two years and can be renewed, serving as a pathway to long-term residency.
visas.target_applicant: This permit is ideal for non-EU/EEA citizens who have secured a job offer from a Lithuanian employer and meet specific qualification, experience, or salary requirements.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After residing in Lithuania for five years with a temporary residence permit, individuals may apply for a permanent residence permit.
visas.renewal_conditions: Application for renewal must be submitted to the Migration Department at least 2 months (general procedure) or 1 month (urgent procedure) before the current permit expires, but no earlier than 4 months prior.
benefits: Legal right to live in Lithuania and travel across the Schengen Area.
Opportunity to work legally for a Lithuanian employer.
Access to Lithuania's healthcare and education systems.
Pathway to permanent residence and citizenship after five years.
Ability to bring family members through reunification.
required_documents: Valid travel document (passport).
Application for issuing/changing a temporary residence permit (submitted electronically via MIGRIS).
Mediation letter submitted electronically by the employer.
Employment contract.
Work permit or a decision from the Employment Service that your work corresponds to the demands of the Lithuanian labor market (if required).
Documents confirming qualifications or relevant work experience (e.g., diplomas, certificates, employment records).
Document proving sufficient funds for subsistence and return (e.g., bank statement, work contract confirming sufficient salary).
Proof of accommodation in Lithuania.
Health insurance valid in Lithuania (sum of 30,000 EUR).
Criminal record certificate (issued within the past six months, from countries lived in).
application_process_steps: Employer finds a candidate and confirms eligibility.
Employer submits a mediation letter through the MIGRIS system, paying a stamp duty.
Applicant fills out an online application form and uploads digital copies of required documents via MIGRIS.

Applicant schedules an appointment via MIGRIS to visit the Migration Department (in Lithuania) or a VFS Global center (abroad) to submit original documents and provide biometric data within 4 months of online submission.
Applicant pays the state fee for the residence permit application.
Migration Department processes the application and issues a decision.
Upon approval, the applicant collects the Temporary Residence Permit and declares their place of residence within one month.

visas.name: EU Blue Card (Temporary Residence Permit for Highly Skilled Workers)
visas.description: The EU Blue Card in Lithuania is an EU-wide work and residence permit specifically designed to attract highly qualified specialists from third countries to the European Union labour market. It allows citizens of non-EU countries to live and work in Lithuania and across the EU under streamlined conditions, providing a faster and easier alternative to a standard work permit.
visas.target_applicant: This permit is for highly qualified non-EU citizens who possess a higher education diploma or equivalent professional experience, have a valid employment contract with a Lithuanian employer, and meet specific salary thresholds.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After holding the EU Blue Card for five continuous years within the European Union, with at least two years legally and continuously in Lithuania, holders may apply for a long-term EU resident status or Lithuanian permanent residency. Basic knowledge of the Lithuanian language and Constitution may be tested.
visas.renewal_conditions: The EU Blue Card can be renewed under the same conditions, requiring the maintenance of the income threshold and continuous employment. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 1 workday before expiry, but no earlier than 6 months prior.
benefits: Fast-track access to the Lithuanian labour market.
Legal work and residence across EU member states.
Eligibility for family reunification under simplified rules.
Longer initial validity of up to 3 years compared to standard temporary residence permits.
Path to permanent residence and EU long-term resident status.
required_documents: Valid Passport (minimum 6 months validity).
Employment Contract (for at least 6 months, confirming position and salary).

Proof of Qualifications: Higher education diploma or professional experience documentation (at least 5 years in the last 7 years, or 3 years for IT specialists, equivalent to higher education qualifications).
Health insurance valid in Lithuania.
Clean criminal record certificate.
Passport-size photos.
Proof of accommodation in Lithuania.
Evidence of salary meeting the threshold.
Translations and legalization of documents where required.
application_process_steps: Secure a valid employment contract with a Lithuanian employer that meets the salary requirements.
Employer submits a Mediation Letter to the Lithuanian Migration Department via the MIGRIS e-service system.
Electronically fill out the EU Blue Card application through the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS) and attach digital copies of required documents.
Schedule an appointment via MIGRIS to personally submit biometric data and original documents at a VFS Global Application Centre abroad or at the Migration Department in Lithuania.
Pay the application fee.
Await decision (can be tracked via MIGRIS); upon approval, collect the temporary residence permit (Blue Card) at a Migration Department office or through an external service provider.

visas.name: National Visa (Type D) for Studies
visas.description: The National Visa (Type D) for Studies in Lithuania is a long-stay visa allowing non-EU/EEA citizens to enter and remain in Lithuania for periods longer than 90 days, specifically for the purpose of full-time study at a recognized higher education institution. This visa serves as the initial entry permit, after which students must apply for a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP) for continued stay.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are non-EU/EEA citizens who have been accepted into a full-time study program at a recognized higher education institution in Lithuania.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The National Visa (D) for Studies allows initial entry to Lithuania. After arrival, students must apply for a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP). The TRP is typically granted for 2 years or the duration of studies and can be renewed. Extended legal residency through TRPs can eventually lead to eligibility for permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The National Visa (D) itself is generally not renewable. For continued stay beyond its validity, a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP) must be applied for while legally residing in Lithuania.
benefits: Allows initial entry and stay in Lithuania for study purposes for up to one year.
Grants access to apply for a Temporary Residence Permit for longer-term studies.
Facilitates travel within the Schengen area for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
Opportunity to study in a European Union country with globally recognized degrees.
required_documents: Completed and signed National Visa Application Form (D-type)
One recent passport-sized color photo (35x45mm, white background)
Valid travel document/passport (at least 2 blank pages, issued within 10 years, valid for at least 3 months beyond intended departure or 6 months beyond requested visa validity)
Mediation letter number from the Lithuanian educational institution, submitted electronically via MIGRIS (Lithuanian Migration Information System)

Proof of sufficient financial means for living expenses (equal to minimum wage, e.g., €1153/month in 2026) and return to home country (e.g., bank statements for the last 3-6 months, stamped and signed by the bank)
Document confirming health insurance (minimum €30,000 coverage, valid in all Schengen Area countries and for the duration of stay)
Confirmed flight reservation/itinerary
Proof of accommodation in Lithuania
Documents providing educational background (duly legalized)
University admission letter
Proof of tuition fee payment or guarantee letter (if required by university)
Police clearance certificate (for first-time Temporary Residence Permit application)
application_process_steps: Receive a formal admission letter from a recognized Lithuanian university.
The university submits a mediation letter electronically via the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS).
Complete the electronic National Visa Application Form (D-type) via MIGRIS.
Gather all required supporting documents, ensuring they are valid and in Lithuanian or English.
Book a visa appointment at a Lithuanian embassy, consulate, or VFS Global center in your home country (or country of legal residence).
Attend the appointment in person to submit the application, supporting documents, provide biometrics, and pay the application fee.
Collect the National Visa (D) upon approval.
Travel to Lithuania and apply for a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP) after arrival, via MIGRIS and in-person at the Migration Department.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Studies
visas.description: This permit is for non-EU/EFTA citizens enrolled in full-time studies at a recognized Lithuanian higher education institution, allowing them to reside temporarily in Lithuania for the duration of their studies. It enables long-term stay exceeding 90 days.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU/EFTA citizens accepted into full-time Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD programs at a Lithuanian educational institution.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Upon graduation, students can apply for an additional 12-month Temporary Residence Permit to seek employment or engage in self-employment in Lithuania, which can then lead to other long-term residence permits based on work or business.
visas.renewal_conditions: Maintaining student status, possessing sufficient funds for subsistence, having valid health insurance, and submitting the application at least 2 months but not earlier than 4 months before the current permit's expiry. A new mediation letter from the educational institution is typically required.
benefits: Right to temporarily reside in Lithuania for the duration of studies, up to 1-2 years (3 years for doctoral students).
Renewable for the remaining study period.
Allows full-time work without hourly restrictions; no additional permits required.
Option to apply for a 12-month post-graduation TRP to seek employment or engage in self-employment.
Master's and doctoral students may bring family members without a waiting period.
required_documents: Valid travel document (passport) with at least three months validity beyond the requested permit's expiration.
University acceptance (Mediation Letter) from the Lithuanian educational institution, confirming acceptance, paid tuition/enrollment fees, and sufficient funds.
Proofs of sufficient funds for subsistence (at least €577 x 12 months + €1153 for return to origin country, totaling €8077) through recent bank statements or a bank certificate.
Health insurance policy with a minimum coverage amount of €10,000 to €30,000, valid for the duration of the TRP.
Document concerning the place of residence in Lithuania or a commitment to declare it upon arrival.
Certificate of Non-Criminal Record/Police Clearance Certificate (for first-time applicants, issued no older than 6 months, translated to Lithuanian, and legalized/apostilled if required).
Digital professional photo.
Copy of previous visa or TRP (if applicable).
application_process_steps: Obtain an acceptance (mediation letter) from a recognized Lithuanian educational institution.
Electronically fill out the Temporary Residence Permit application form through the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS) at migracija.lt.
Upload digital copies of all required documents to the MIGRIS system.
Book an appointment through MIGRIS to visit the Migration Department in person (if in Lithuania) or a VFS Global center (if abroad) within 4 months of online submission.
Attend the appointment to submit original documents, provide biometric data, and pay the state fee.
Await the decision on the Temporary Residence Permit application.

visas.name: National Visa (Type D) for Business/Investment
visas.description: The National Visa (Type D) for Business/Investment in Lithuania is a long-term visa designed for non-EU entrepreneurs, company directors, and investors planning an extended stay in Lithuania for business activities. It allows individuals to reside in Lithuania for more than 90 days, typically up to one year, to establish, manage, or invest in a Lithuanian company, serving as a precursor to applying for a Temporary Residence Permit.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are non-EU entrepreneurs and investors seeking to establish, purchase, or manage a company in Lithuania, aiming for a long-term presence and potential future residency in the country.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The National Visa (Type D) for Business/Investment serves as a precursor to obtaining a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP). After entering Lithuania on the D visa and commencing business activity, applicants can apply for a TRP. Key conditions for TRP include the business being operational for at least six months and employing at least two full-time Lithuanian or EU citizens with a combined gross monthly salary of at least €4,500. The initial TRP is typically valid for one to two years and can be extended, leading to eligibility for permanent residency after approximately five to six years of continuous legal residence.
visas.renewal_conditions: The National Visa (Type D) itself is not directly renewable; after its expiry, a 180-day waiting period is generally required before another can be issued. The recommended pathway for long-term stay is to transition to a Temporary Residence Permit.
benefits: Allows for stays exceeding 90 days, up to 12 months, in Lithuania.
Provides a legal pathway to apply for a Temporary Residence Permit in Lithuania.
Enables active participation in managing or investing in a Lithuanian company.
Facilitates access to the broader European Union market for business operations.
required_documents: Valid travel document (passport) issued within the last 10 years, with at least two blank pages, and valid for at least three months beyond the requested visa's validity period.
Electronically filled and submitted national long-term visa application via the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS).
Mediation letter (invitation) from a Lithuanian company, submitted electronically through MIGRIS by the inviting entity.
Document for the establishment or acquisition of an undertaking in Lithuania, established not earlier than one year before the application date.
Document confirming that the value of the company's equity amounts to at least €28,000.
Document confirming applicant's membership in the company and investment of at least €14,000 of funds or assets into the company.
Proof of sufficient means of subsistence (e.g., personal bank account statement showing at least €6,000).
Health insurance document valid in Lithuania and all Schengen countries, with minimum coverage of €30,000.
One 35x45mm size colored and age-appropriate photograph.
Clean criminal record certificate from the country of origin or residence.
application_process_steps: Establish or purchase a Lithuanian company (e.g., UAB) with a minimum share capital of €28,000, ensuring the applicant holds at least one-third of the shares and invests at least €14,000.
Obtain a mediation letter (invitation) from the Lithuanian company, which must be submitted electronically through the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS) by the inviting entity.
Fill out and submit the national long-term visa application electronically via MIGRIS.
Gather all required supporting documents, including a valid passport, proof of financial means, health insurance, and a clean criminal record certificate.
Schedule an appointment at a Lithuanian embassy or consulate abroad, an authorized visa center, or a territorial division of the Migration Department if already legally present in Lithuania.
Attend the appointment, submit original documents, pay the application fee, and provide biometric data (fingerprints and a digital photo).
Await the decision on the visa application, which typically takes 15 calendar days but can be extended up to 45 days.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit by Investment (Business Investment Route)
visas.description: This permit allows non-EU nationals to reside in Lithuania by investing in or establishing a Lithuanian company and actively participating in its business activities. It grants the right to live, work, and study in Lithuania and travel freely within the Schengen Area.
visas.target_applicant: Entrepreneurs, investors, and business owners from non-EU countries looking to establish or acquire a company in Lithuania, actively manage it, and contribute to the local economy.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After holding a Temporary Residence Permit for 5 consecutive years, holders are eligible to apply for Permanent Residency. Citizenship by naturalization becomes available after 10 years of continuous legal residence, requiring proof of stable income, compliance with immigration regulations, no serious criminal history, basic Lithuanian language proficiency, and knowledge of the Lithuanian constitution and national anthem.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain active business operations, satisfy employment requirements (e.g., employing Lithuanian/EU citizens with required salaries), and continue to meet all eligibility criteria.
visas.tax_implications: Lithuania applies a progressive personal income tax system (20% for income up to €126,532/year, 32% above). Investment income (dividends, capital gains, royalties, interest) up to €253,065 annually is taxed at a flat rate of 15%. A 2025 investment account regime allows tax deferral on qualifying investments.
benefits: Right to live, work, and study in Lithuania.
Visa-free travel across the 27 Schengen Area member states.
Opportunity to bring spouse and dependent children.
Access to a business-friendly environment with low taxes.
Path to permanent residency after 5 years and citizenship after 10 years of continuous legal residence.
required_documents: Valid passport
Completed application form (via MIGRIS)
Purpose-specific documents (e.g., company registration, investment proof, business plan, employment contracts)
Proof of accommodation in Lithuania
Health insurance with minimum coverage of €30,000
Proof of sufficient personal living funds (€1,038 per month for 12 months)
Clean criminal record certificate (issued within the past six months, from all countries of residence)
Legalized and translated documents (if applicable)
Biometric data (fingerprints and digital photo)
application_process_steps: Select the preferred investment route (establish a new company, acquire an existing business, or open a branch).
Register or purchase the company, obtain incorporation documents, register with the State Tax Inspectorate, and open a local business bank account.
Obtain a National Visa D (if required, e.g., for establishing a new company) and commence business activity.
Prepare all necessary documents, including business plan, proof of funds, company ownership documents, criminal record certificate, and health insurance.
Submit the Temporary Residence Permit application to the Lithuanian Migration Department (online via MIGRIS) or a Lithuanian consulate abroad.
Await approval. The Migration Department assesses eligibility and verifies documents; additional information may be requested.

visas.name: Startup Visa (Temporary Residence Permit for Entrepreneurs)
visas.description: The Lithuania Startup Visa is a government initiative allowing non-EU entrepreneurs to obtain a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP) to launch and grow innovative businesses in Lithuania. It provides a streamlined path for founders with scalable, technology-based ideas to reside and work in the country, fostering economic and social development.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU citizens with an innovative, technology-based, and scalable business idea who intend to establish and actively manage a startup in Lithuania.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 5 years of continuous legal residence on a Temporary Residence Permit, applicants are eligible to apply for Permanent Residency. Citizenship by naturalization becomes available after 10 years of continuous legal residence, subject to passing Lithuanian language and Constitution examinations.
visas.renewal_conditions: Evidence of business progress and growth, full tax and fee payments, and a positive evaluation by the startup committee.
benefits: Visa-free travel across the Schengen zone.
Full-time work rights for the spouse and free public education for children.
Access to a growing startup ecosystem and potential government-backed grants.
Path to permanent residency after 5 years and citizenship after 10 years.
Lower cost of living compared to many other European countries.
required_documents: Valid passport
Completed TRP application form
Passport-sized photographs
Detailed business plan (innovative, technology-based, scalable concept, development strategy, financial projections, market analysis)
Proof of sufficient funds for living expenses (€12,456 for one year for one person)
Health insurance policy with at least €30,000 coverage valid in Lithuania
Police clearance certificates from any country of residence for the last 2 years (if resided for more than 6 months)
Official confirmation letter from Enterprise Lithuania (after business idea approval)
Proof of accommodation in Lithuania
application_process_steps: Prepare a detailed business plan outlining the innovative, scalable business idea.
Submit an online application with personal details, team, product, and business plan to the Startup Lithuania platform.
Participate in an online video interview if the application is pre-approved.
Await evaluation by the Lithuanian Startup Committee for approval of the business idea.
Receive an official endorsement letter from Enterprise Lithuania upon approval.
Apply for a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP) at the Lithuanian Migration Department or a Lithuanian embassy, submitting the required documents and the endorsement letter.
Register a company in Lithuania, such as a Private Limited Liability Company (UAB), within 120 days of relocation or 30 days of TRP approval.

visas.name: National Visa (Type D) for Family Reunification
visas.description: The National Visa (Type D) for Family Reunification in Lithuania allows non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals to enter and stay in Lithuania for up to one year to join a family member legally residing in the country. This visa serves as an entry permit and a bridge to apply for a Temporary Residence Permit for long-term family reunification.
visas.target_applicant: Immediate family members (spouses, minor children, and dependent parents) of Lithuanian citizens or non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals holding a valid residence permit in Lithuania, particularly those of researchers, teachers, or highly qualified workers.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The National Visa (Type D) for Family Reunification allows entry and stay in Lithuania for up to one year. During this period, the visa holder can apply for a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP) for family reunification while remaining in Lithuania. The TRP is initially issued for one year and is renewable annually, leading to eligibility for permanent residence after five years of continuous legal stay. After seven years of residence, family members may be eligible to apply for Lithuanian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The National Visa (D) itself is generally not directly renewable for continuous stay; another national visa can only be issued if more than 180 days have passed since the expiration of the previous one. However, it is intended as a stepping stone to apply for a Temporary Residence Permit for longer stays, which is renewable.
benefits: Legal entry and stay in Lithuania for up to 12 months.
Ability to apply for a Temporary Residence Permit while remaining in Lithuania.
Path to long-term residency and eventually citizenship via the Temporary Residence Permit.
Access to healthcare, education, and social services upon obtaining a residence permit.
Possibility of multiple entries into Lithuania during the visa's validity.
required_documents: Completed electronic National (D) visa application form.
Valid travel document (passport) issued within the last 10 years, with at least two blank pages and validity for at least three months beyond the requested visa period.
One recent color photograph (35x45 mm) with a white background.
Proof of familial relationship (e.g., marriage certificate, birth certificate).

Proof of sufficient financial means to support oneself (at least one minimum monthly wage per month of stay, plus funds for return, €1153 as of 2026). This can be a bank statement or employment contract.
Health insurance document valid in Lithuania and all Schengen countries, with a minimum coverage of €30,000.
Proof of accommodation in Lithuania.

Certificate(s) from competent authorities of foreign state(s) where the applicant lived for the last 2 years, confirming conviction status (or a written statement if not convicted) (primarily for TRP, but advisable for D visa).
application_process_steps: Complete the application electronically via the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS).
Include digital copies of all required documents.
Pay the application fee.
Book an appointment at a Lithuanian embassy/consulate abroad or a Migration Department territorial division if legally in Lithuania.
Attend the appointment in person to submit original documents, provide biometric data (fingerprints), and undergo an interview if required.
Await the decision on the visa application, typically within 15-45 calendar days.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Family Reunification
visas.description: The Temporary Residence Permit for Family Reunification in Lithuania allows non-EU citizens to live with their close family members who are either Lithuanian citizens or foreign nationals holding a valid Lithuanian residence permit. This permit grants long-term residency in Lithuania.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals who wish to join their spouse, registered partner, minor children, or dependent parents/grandparents in Lithuania, where the sponsoring family member is a Lithuanian citizen or holds a valid Lithuanian residence permit.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Years spent in Lithuania on a Temporary Residence Permit count towards the residency requirement for a Permanent Residence Permit, which typically requires 5 years of continuous legal residence. After 7 years of residence, family members may be eligible to apply for Lithuanian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit is renewable provided eligibility criteria continue to be met. Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 2 months, but not earlier than 4 months, before the current permit expires. If the sponsor is a Lithuanian citizen or a permanent resident, the permit is initially issued for 1 year and renewed for 2 years. If the sponsor holds a TRP, the family member's TRP is granted for the same period as the sponsor's.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of a Temporary Residence Permit for Family Reunification, if deemed tax residents, are generally taxed on their worldwide income. There are no specific special tax treatments for this visa category; standard Lithuanian resident tax rules apply. Gifts and inheritances from close relatives are exempt from tax.
benefits: Right to reside long-term in Lithuania.
Access to healthcare, education, and social services.
Right to work in Lithuania without needing a separate work permit.
Visa-free travel within the Schengen Area for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
Pathway to permanent residency after a qualifying period of continuous residence.
required_documents: Application for issuing a temporary residence permit
Valid travel document (passport) valid for at least three months longer than the requested permit validity
Proof of existence of the family relationship (e.g., marriage certificate, birth certificate)
Documents confirming sufficient financial resources for applicant and family members
Proof of adequate accommodation (at least 7 square meters per adult)
Health insurance covering emergency medical care and repatriation expenses (minimum 6000 EUR coverage is mentioned in some sources)

Criminal record certificate from countries of previous residence for the last 2 years (issued no earlier than six months before application date), or a written statement of no conviction (for first-time applicants joining a highly-qualified worker)
List of trips and stays in foreign states
Biometric data (fingerprints and facial photograph)
Original documents for all foreign-issued records, with Apostille certification and certified Lithuanian translation where required
application_process_steps: Submit the Temporary Residence Permit application online via the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS) and upload all required documents.
Book an appointment at the Migration Department through MIGRIS within 4 months of online submission.

Attend the in-person appointment at the Migration Department (or VFS Global office abroad) to submit original documents, provide biometric data (fingerprints and facial photograph), and pay the application fee.
Undergo security verification by relevant state authorities.
Receive notification of the decision via email.
Collect the Temporary Residence Permit card from the Migration Department (or VFS Global office).
Formally declare your place of residence within 1 month of receiving the TRP card.

visas.name: National Visa (Type D) for Researchers and Teachers (with family members)
visas.description: The National Visa (Type D) for Researchers and Teachers in Lithuania is designed for foreign nationals who intend to come to Lithuania for scientific research or teaching activities at a registered science and studies institution. This visa allows for a long-term stay in the Republic of Lithuania, exceeding 90 days, and permits family members to accompany the primary applicant.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are researchers and teachers who have secured an employment or authorship contract with a Lithuanian science and research institution, or are involved in joint governmental programs, along with their immediate family members.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The National Visa (D) for researchers and teachers serves as a precursor to a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP). Researchers and teachers, along with their family members, can apply for a TRP to continue their stay in Lithuania. After five years of continuous legal residence in Lithuania (typically on a TRP), one may apply for permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The National Visa (D) itself is generally not directly renewable for a consecutive year. A new National Visa (D) can only be issued if more than 180 days have passed since the expiration of the previous one. For continuous stay, applicants are expected to apply for a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP) before their National Visa (D) expires.
benefits: Allows entry and a long-term stay in Lithuania for up to 12 months.
Permits travel within the Schengen Area for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
Enables family members (spouse, minor children) to join the primary applicant in Lithuania.
Provides a pathway to obtaining a Temporary Residence Permit for continued stay and potential permanent residency.
required_documents: Completed National Visa application form submitted electronically via MIGRIS (Lithuanian Migration Information System).
Valid travel document (passport) issued within the last 10 years, with at least two blank pages, and valid for at least three months beyond the requested visa's validity period.
One recent color photograph (35x45mm, white background).
Mediation letter (request to issue a multiple-entry national visa) submitted electronically by the inviting Lithuanian institution via MIGRIS/EPIS.
Employment contract or authorship contract with a Lithuanian science and studies institution.

Proof of sufficient financial means for living expenses (equal to at least one minimum monthly wage, currently €1153) for the entire duration of the visa and for return to the home country (equal to one minimum monthly wage).
Health insurance document valid in Lithuania and all Schengen countries, with a minimum coverage of €30,000.
Proof of accommodation for the duration of the intended stay.
Flight/travel reservations or other proof of intended transport.
Criminal record certificate, legalized or apostilled according to legal procedures.
Proof of applicant's legal status in the country of residence (if applying from a country other than the country of citizenship).
application_process_steps: Complete the national visa application form electronically via the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS).
Upload digital copies of all required supporting documents to the MIGRIS system.
Book an appointment at a Lithuanian diplomatic mission or consular post abroad, or at the Migration Department in Lithuania if already legally present.
Pay the application fee of EUR 140.
Attend the scheduled appointment to submit biometric data (fingerprints and photo) and provide the original documents for verification.
Wait for the decision on the visa application, which is typically made within 15 calendar days, but may be extended to 45 calendar days.

visas.name: National Visa (Type D) for Athletes and Coaches (with family members)
visas.description: The National Visa (Type D) for Athletes and Coaches in Lithuania is a long-stay visa allowing foreign athletes and coaches participating in high-level sports activities to reside in Lithuania for more than 90 days, for a maximum period of one year. This visa category also permits accompanying family members to join the principal applicant.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a professional athlete or coach coming to Lithuania to engage in sports activities, as defined by the Law on Sports of the Republic of Lithuania, and intending to stay for an extended period beyond 90 days, along with their immediate family members.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The National Visa (Type D) for athletes and coaches serves as an initial entry and long-term stay permit. For continuous legal residence beyond the national visa's validity, applicants are generally required to apply for a Temporary Residence Permit. After five years of continuous legal residence in Lithuania with temporary residence permits, individuals may become eligible to apply for a permanent residence permit.
visas.renewal_conditions: A national visa (D) itself is generally not directly renewable. If a 1-year national visa was granted, another national visa can only be issued if more than 180 days have passed since the expiration of the previous one. However, if an applicant applies for a temporary residence permit, a new national visa can be issued for up to 5 months to allow the applicant to stay in Lithuania while the residence permit application is being processed.
benefits: Allows legal stay in Lithuania for up to one year.
Permits the visa holder to engage in sports activities (work) in Lithuania.
Enables family members (spouse and children) to join the athlete or coach.
Provides a pathway to apply for a temporary residence permit for longer stays.
Allows short-term travel within the Schengen area.
required_documents: Completed electronic application form via MIGRIS system
Valid travel document (passport, issued within last 10 years, at least 2 blank pages, valid for at least 3 months beyond visa validity)
One recent color ID photograph (3.5 x 4.5 cm, face occupying 70-80% of area)

Proof of financial stability (e.g., employment contract, bank statement showing funds equal to at least one minimum monthly wage for each month of stay plus one minimum monthly wage for return funds - €1153 monthly, €14989 for a 12-month visa as of 2026)
Health insurance document valid in Lithuania and all Schengen countries, with coverage of at least €30,000

Mediation letter (electronic request to issue a multiple-entry national visa) from the inviting sports institution/organization in Lithuania, submitted via the Information System of Electronic Services (EPIS)
Contract signed with a sports institution registered in the Republic of Lithuania
Documents proving family relation for accompanying family members
Criminal record certificate (must be legalized or apostilled)
Proof of accommodation for the entire duration of the intended stay
application_process_steps: Complete the application electronically via the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS) and include digital copies of required documents.
The inviting sports institution submits a mediation letter electronically via the Information System of Electronic Services (EPIS).
Book an appointment at a Lithuanian visa service abroad (e.g., external service provider like VFS Global) or at the Migration Department in Lithuania if legally present.
Attend the appointment, submit biometric data, and provide original required documents.
Pay the application fee.
Await the decision on the visa application.

visas.name: National Visa (Type D) for Seasonal Workers (over 90 days)
visas.description: This visa is for non-EU citizens who wish to undertake seasonal employment in Lithuania for a period exceeding 90 days. It allows the holder to stay and work in Lithuania for the duration of their seasonal work permit, typically up to 6 months within a 12-month period, although the visa itself can be valid for up to one year.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a non-EU citizen who has secured a seasonal work offer from a Lithuanian employer and obtained a seasonal work permit from the Employment Service for a period longer than 90 days.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Seasonal workers are not entitled to obtain permanent resident's status directly through this visa. For longer stays exceeding 6 months or beyond the seasonal work period, individuals need to apply for a temporary residence permit based on employment.
visas.renewal_conditions: A national (D) visa cannot be immediately obtained after expiration. One must wait at least 180 days after the end of a previous D-visa before being issued a new one. The right to work under a seasonal permit is limited to 6 months per year.
benefits: Allows legal employment in Lithuania for seasonal work.
Permits stay in Lithuania for the duration of the seasonal work permit (up to 6 months per year).
Provides a pathway for non-EU citizens to gain work experience in Lithuania.
Relatively straightforward application process once a work permit is secured.
required_documents: Completed electronic national visa application form.
Valid travel document (passport) with at least 3 months validity beyond the visa issuing date.
One recent color photograph (35 x 45 mm) with white background.
Seasonal work permit or a letter from the local Employment Service Office confirming application for a seasonal work permit.
Mediation letter (reference number) submitted electronically by the employer through MIGRIS.
Proof of sufficient financial resources to support oneself during the stay (e.g., up-to-date personal bank statement for the last 6 months, showing at least one minimal salary per month of stay).
Health insurance policy covering the entire period of stay, valid for the Schengen area, with a minimum cover of EUR 30,000 for medical expenses and repatriation.
Copy of the employment contract.
Proof of accommodation.
Flight reservation (may be required).
Previous passports covering the last 7 years (if applicable, with translated Certificate of movements).
Police clearance certificates (if applicable).
application_process_steps: The employer notifies the job vacancy to the local Employment Service Office.
The employer applies for a seasonal work permit at the local Employment Service Office, submitting a preliminary employment contract.
Once a seasonal work permit is issued (within 7 working days), the employer submits a mediation letter electronically through the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS).

The applicant completes the national visa application electronically through MIGRIS, includes digital copies of required documents, and then books an appointment at a Lithuanian embassy/consulate abroad or the Migration Department in Lithuania if already legally present.
The applicant attends the appointment, pays the visa fee, submits biometric data, and provides original documents.
The visa is processed, typically within 15-30 days, but can extend up to 60 calendar days in complex cases.

visas.name: National Visa (Type D) for Posted Workers
visas.description: The National Visa (Type D) for Posted Workers in Lithuania is a long-stay visa designed for third-country nationals who are posted to work in Lithuania by a company from a non-EU or EFTA country. This visa allows the holder to enter and stay in Lithuania for a period exceeding 90 days, typically up to 12 months, for the purpose of carrying out specific work activities. It often serves as an initial authorization before transitioning to a temporary residence permit for longer stays.
visas.target_applicant: Third-country nationals (non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens) who are assigned by their employer to work temporarily in Lithuania for a specific project or service provision, requiring a stay longer than 90 days.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The National Visa (Type D) serves as a preparatory step for obtaining a temporary residence permit in Lithuania. During the validity of the national visa, or even before its expiry (2-4 months prior), individuals can apply for a temporary residence permit to reside and work in Lithuania for a longer duration, typically up to two years, which can then be renewed.
visas.renewal_conditions: A National Visa (Type D) itself is not directly renewable. A new National Visa (D) may be issued only if more than 180 days have passed since the expiration of a previous one. For continued stay and work beyond 12 months, applicants typically need to apply for a temporary residence permit in Lithuania.
benefits: Legal entry and stay in Lithuania for over 90 days, up to one year.
Permission to engage in the specific work activities for which the visa was granted.
Potential for multiple entries into Lithuania during the visa's validity.
Limited mobility within the Schengen Area for short stays.
Serves as a stepping stone towards obtaining a temporary residence permit for longer-term stay.
required_documents: A National Visa (D) application form, completed electronically via MIGRIS.
A valid travel document (passport) issued within the last 10 years, with at least two blank pages, and valid for at least three months beyond the visa's requested validity period.
One recent color passport photo (35x45 mm, white background).
An electronic mediation letter from the employer in Lithuania, submitted through MIGRIS, with its reference number.
A valid work permit issued by the Employment Service (if required for the specific posting).
A certified copy of a service provision or work performance agreement between the Lithuanian company and the posting company, detailing terms, remuneration, and working hours.
A certified copy of the posting company's registration certificate or an extract from its register.
A certified copy of the employment agreement between the third-country national and the posting company.

A document from a competent authority in the country of the posted employee confirming at least three months of employment and social insurance coverage with the posting company, and the obligation to maintain social insurance during the mission in Lithuania. (If not available, a statement from the posting company and a document confirming no arrears in social security tax).
Proof of qualifications for the job (e.g., diplomas, training certificates, employment record).

Proof of sufficient financial means for living expenses in Lithuania (at least one minimum monthly wage per month of stay) and for returning to the home country (at least one minimum monthly wage for return funds). Current minimum wage in 2026 is €1153/month.
Valid health insurance policy with coverage of at least EUR 30,000, valid in Lithuania and all Schengen countries, covering repatriation costs.
Police clearance certificates or certificate of criminal check (if applicable).
application_process_steps: The Lithuanian company accepting the posted worker must obtain a work permit from the Employment Service (if required) and submit an electronic mediation letter through the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS).
The applicant (posted worker) completes the National Visa (D) application form electronically through MIGRIS and uploads digital copies of all required documents.
The applicant pays the visa application fee.

The applicant books an appointment to submit biometric data (if required) and present original documents at a Lithuanian embassy or consulate abroad, or at a Migration Department territorial division if legally in Lithuania.
The application is processed, and a decision is made within the specified timeframe.

visas.name: National Visa (Type D) for Governmental Program Participants
visas.description: This visa is for foreigners participating in joint governmental programs with Lithuania, typically as teachers or researchers, or for athletes and coaches involved in high-level sports activities. It allows for a long-term stay in Lithuania for up to one year.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are teachers or researchers engaged in joint government programs with a foreign country, or high-level athletes and coaches coming to Lithuania for sports, including their family members. It also covers participants in certain youth exchange programs.
visas.path_to_residency_description: While a National Visa (Type D) is for long-term stays, for continued long-term residence, holders will generally need to apply for a Temporary Residence Permit (TRP) in Lithuania. The National Visa can serve as the legal basis for staying in Lithuania while the TRP application is processed.
visas.renewal_conditions: A multiple-entry national visa for one year may be issued, and another multiple-entry national visa can be issued if more than 180 days have passed since the expiry of the previous visa. If an application for a residence permit is submitted, a national visa may be issued for a maximum of 5 months from the date of application.
benefits: Allows a long-term stay in Lithuania for up to one year.
Family members (spouse, children) may also be eligible for the visa if accompanying eligible teachers/researchers or athletes/coaches.
Potential for temporary residence and work permits for youth exchange participants upon arrival.
Permits multiple entries into Lithuania during its validity period.
Can be a stepping stone for longer-term residence permits in Lithuania.
required_documents: Completed electronic national visa application form (via MIGRIS)
Valid travel document (passport, issued within last 10 years, with at least two blank pages, and validity at least 3 months longer than the requested visa)
Color photo corresponding to the applicant's age

Documents indicating the purpose of the journey (e.g., official invitation for governmental program, employment contract for teachers/researchers, documents confirming participation in sports activities)

Proof of sufficient means of subsistence (at least 1 minimum monthly salary for each month of stay, plus funds for return, e.g., bank statement, employment contract). The minimum monthly salary is EUR 924 as of January 1, 2024.
Health insurance document, valid in Lithuania and all Schengen countries, with a minimum coverage of EUR 30,000
Proof of accommodation for the entire duration of the intended stay
Criminal record certificate (Police Clearance Certificate)
Documents confirming family relationship, if applying with dependants
application_process_steps: Complete the electronic application for a national visa via the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS - migracija.lt).
Upload digital copies of all required supporting documents.
Book an appointment for submission of documents and biometric data.

Attend the appointment at the Lithuanian visa service in a foreign country (or external service provider) or the Migration Department in Lithuania, submit original documents, and provide biometric data.
Pay the application fee of EUR 140 (unless exempt).
Await the decision, which is typically made within 15 to 30 calendar days, but can be extended up to 60 days in exceptional cases.

visas.name: National Visa (Type D) for Medical Treatment, Unforeseen Reasons, or Force Majeure
visas.description: This National Visa (Type D) allows foreigners to enter and stay in Lithuania for a period longer than 90 days, up to a maximum of 12 months. It is specifically intended for individuals who are unable to leave Lithuania due to compelling circumstances such as serious illness, other acute health disorders, unforeseen personal reasons, or force majeure.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a foreigner who is currently in Lithuania and cannot depart the country due to unforeseen and uncontrollable circumstances like medical emergencies, significant personal events, or force majeure, requiring an extended legal stay.
visas.path_to_residency_description: While the National Visa (D) itself is not a direct path to permanent residency, it can serve as a stepping stone to a temporary residence permit. After five years of continuous legal residence in Lithuania (often through temporary residence permits), an individual may become eligible for a permanent residence permit.
visas.renewal_conditions: A new national visa D may be issued if more than 180 days have passed since the expiration of the previous visa. If an application for a temporary residence permit is submitted, a national visa may be issued for a maximum of 5 months to cover the processing period.
benefits: Legal stay in Lithuania for more than 90 days, up to 12 months.
Allows for multiple entries and exits from Lithuania during its validity period.
Provides limited mobility within the Schengen area for short stays.
Can serve as a temporary bridge for those applying for a temporary residence permit.
required_documents: Completed electronic national visa application form via MIGRIS.
Valid travel document (passport) issued within the last 10 years, with at least two blank pages, and valid for at least three months beyond the requested visa's validity period.
One recent color photograph (35 x 45 mm) with a white background.

Proof of sufficient financial stability to cover living expenses (at least €1153 per month for 2026) for the entire stay and funds for return (equal to 1 minimum monthly wage), e.g., bank statement, employment contract.

Health insurance valid in Lithuania and all Schengen countries, with a minimum coverage of €30,000 for medical expenses, urgent medical attention, emergency hospital treatment, repatriation for medical reasons (including escort), and death.

Documents proving the reason for inability to leave Lithuania (e.g., medical certificates from relevant organizations for illness, official statements for unforeseen personal reasons or force majeure).
application_process_steps: Complete the national visa application form electronically via the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS).
Include digital copies of all required documents in MIGRIS.
Book an appointment for submission.

Attend the scheduled appointment at an external service provider (if abroad) or the Migration Department (if legally in Lithuania), submit biometric data, and provide original copies of the attached application documents.
Pay the application fee.

visas.name: Permanent Residence Permit
visas.description: The Permanent Residence Permit (also known as a Permit of a Long-term Resident of the Republic of Lithuania to Reside in the European Union) grants foreign nationals the right to live, work, and study in Lithuania indefinitely, providing long-term stability and nearly the same rights as Lithuanian citizens, with the exception of voting and holding certain public offices. It confirms the alien's permanent resident status.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU citizens who have legally resided in Lithuania on a valid temporary residence permit for at least five consecutive years, and citizens of EU/EEA states and their family members who have lived legally and continuously in Lithuania for the same period.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After obtaining permanent residence and fulfilling additional requirements, such as maintaining legal residence for a total of 10 years (including the 5 years on permanent residency), demonstrating proficiency in the Lithuanian language and Constitution, and having a stable income, individuals may apply for Lithuanian citizenship by naturalization.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit is issued for 5 years and must be replaced after this period. The applicant must continue to meet the grounds for residence.
visas.tax_implications: Standard Lithuanian tax residency rules apply. Tax residency is triggered by spending at least 183 days in Lithuania in a tax year, or 280 days across two consecutive years with at least 90 days in either year. Tax residents are liable on worldwide income, while non-tax residents are taxed only on income sourced within Lithuania.
benefits: Right to live in Lithuania without any time-limit tied to the permit
Ability to work in Lithuania and to establish a business without extra employment permits
Access to public healthcare and education systems under the same conditions as Lithuanian citizens
Eligibility to participate in social security and pension schemes
Freedom of travel within the Schengen Area
required_documents: Valid passport
Completed application form (submitted via MIGRIS)
Documents confirming the right of permanent residence (e.g., proof of long-term residence, marriage certificate, proof of Lithuanian descent)
Proof of legal residence for the five years (entry/exit records, permit renewals)
Income statements and tax records demonstrating financial self-sufficiency for at least one year
Accommodation proof (ownership, lease, or registered accommodation agreement)
Health insurance policy or confirmation of enrollment
Certificate of clean criminal record from Lithuania and any prior country of residence (if applicant is older than 14 years, issued no earlier than six months before application)
Certificate of Lithuanian language competence (A2 level)
Certificate of knowledge of the Lithuanian Constitution
Proof of paid state fee for the residence permit
Biometric data (photo, fingerprints)
Original documents for all foreign-issued records, with Apostille certification and certified Lithuanian translation where required
application_process_steps: Verify eligibility and gather all required documentation.
Submit the application form and upload digital copies of documents through the Lithuanian Migration Information System (MIGRIS).

Schedule an appointment at the Migration Department (or an external service provider if applying from abroad) to provide biometric data (photo, fingerprints) and submit original documents within 4 months of the online application submission.
Wait for the review process and decision on the application.
Collect the permanent residence permit once the application is approved.

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Lithuanian citizenship by descent is available to individuals who can prove that at least one of their parents, grandparents, or great-grandparents was a citizen of the Republic of Lithuania before June 15, 1940 (prior to Soviet occupation), and emigrated before March 11, 1990. Acceptable documentation includes Lithuanian passports, birth certificates, military records, or other official documents from the 1918-1940 period. Dual citizenship is permitted in these cases, especially if the ancestor emigrated to a country outside the former Soviet Union. The application process involves gathering extensive documents, often requiring archive research, and submitting them to the Migration Department.

Naturalization.desc: Naturalization is an option for individuals who do not qualify by descent. Applicants must generally reside in Lithuania for 5 to 10 years uninterruptedly, be adults, have no criminal convictions, master the state language (requiring an A2 or B1 level exam depending on the role), and pass an exam on the fundamentals of the Lithuanian Constitution. Proof of sufficient means of subsistence is also required.

Birthright.desc: Citizenship by birthright (jus soli) is not generally applied in Lithuania. However, a person can acquire Lithuanian citizenship by being born to a Lithuanian parent, regardless of the place of birth (jus sanguinis).

Spouse and Family.desc: Spouses of Lithuanian citizens may be eligible for Lithuanian citizenship through naturalization after 7 years of residency in the country. However, a spouse cannot claim citizenship solely through their partner's Lithuanian ancestry; they would need to qualify independently through their own ancestors or standard naturalization.

tax_advice:
*   **Corporate Income Tax (CIT):** As of January 1, 2025, the standard CIT rate increased from 15% to 16%. The preferential CIT rate for small companies, cooperatives, and R&D businesses increased from 5% to 6%. A reduced rate of 1% applies to agricultural cooperative companies' taxable profits. Specific exemptions for healthcare and insurance providers have been removed.
*   **Personal Income Tax (PIT):** Lithuania applies a competitive flat rate of 15% on most income up to €90,246 (2024 rates). Progressive rates apply for higher earners: 20% on income between €90,246 and €195,096, and 32% on income exceeding €195,096. Employers withhold tax monthly through the PAYE system.
*   **Capital Gains & Dividends:** Generally taxed at a flat 15%. An annual tax-free amount of €500 applies to interest income, with exemptions for certain government bonds. Capital gains from selling securities held over one year may qualify for reduced taxation. As of 2025, investment returns will be taxed only upon withdrawal from investment accounts.
*   **Social Security Contributions:** Employees contribute 19.50% of their gross salary to social security.
*   **Value Added Tax (VAT):** The annual income threshold for VAT registration is expected to rise from €45,000 to €55,000 in 2025, based on the calendar year. The reduced VAT rate increased from 9% to 12%, while the reduced VAT rate for books decreased from 9% to 5%. The zero percent VAT rate for central heating was eliminated.
*   **Other Taxes:** A 'security tax' of 10% on non-life insurance policy premiums (excluding mandatory drivers' civil liability insurance) was introduced to fund the State Defence Fund.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Compared to Western Europe, Lithuania remains notably cheaper, though prices have increased in recent years, especially for housing and dining in city centers. A single person can live comfortably on €1,200-€1,800 per month, while a family of four might expect to spend €2,800-€4,000. Rent for a one-room apartment in the city center is about €610, and in remote areas around €400. A two-bedroom apartment in central Vilnius costs €600-€800 monthly.
*   **Language:** The official language is Lithuanian, which can be challenging to learn. From January 1, 2026, foreign workers in direct service roles (selling goods or pouring coffee) must demonstrate at least A1 level proficiency in Lithuanian. This requirement applies after two years of residence for those whose permits were issued before December 31, 2025, or two years from the first issuance of a residence document for others. After this two-year period, A2 level proficiency will be required for continued work in the service and trade sector. Taking a formal language exam is necessary, as course completion certificates are not sufficient.
*   **Safety:** Lithuania consistently ranks among the safest countries in Europe, with low crime rates in major cities like Vilnius, Kaunas, and Klaipėda.
*   **Registration & Residency:** Non-nationals need a separate permit to work and reside in Lithuania. Temporary residence permits are typically issued for one to two years and cost around €160. Applicants need to show at least €840 in the bank and a clean criminal record. Digital nomads can obtain a one-year renewable visa, requiring employment with a non-Lithuanian company or self-employment for non-Lithuanian clients, a minimum monthly income of €3,857 (2024), health insurance, and proof of accommodation.
*   **Work Culture:** While a growing job market exists, especially in IT, fintech, and business services, some expats report a potentially toxic work culture in local companies, recommending international employers.
